transcript:
Header: 
Date: 2027-06-30
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Dana (Catalyst CTO), Peter (Catalyst ML), Sofia (Catalyst Infra)

Summary (auto):
Quick discovery focusing on model selection for Catalyst's multi-lingual customer support assistant. Topics: context length needs (long transcripts ~100k tokens), open model tradeoffs, tool/function-calling for live API lookups, hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment options, security/compliance. Agreed to run a live benchmark with sample transcripts and share SOC2 + dedicated pricing.

Topics: model families, quantization, context length, tool calling, multilingual performance, deployment mode tradeoffs

Transcript:
00:00 Aisha: hey everyone thanks for joining, um quick intros?
00:07 Dana: yeah dana here, cto, we run the support assistant for multi-lingual corporate customers
00:12 Peter: peter ml eng, doing model selection and evals
00:16 Sofia: sofia infra, looking at networking and security needs
00:20 Aisha: great, marco from our infra team will do the deep tech dive a bit later on. marco?
00:28 Marco: hi all, uh quick agenda, we'll cover model choices (open models vs managed), context windows, multilingual behavior, function/tool calling, and deployment options hosted / dedicated / private then Q&A
00:45 Dana: perfect, our main constraint is we process long call transcripts, some up to 150k tokens, typical 60k, and we need to maintain context for follow-ups. Also we need spanish, portuguese, japanese support and tool calls to call our internal CRM when responding.
01:05 Marco: okay so two axis here: model architecture and runtime. for 60-150k context today you generally need either chunking + KV cache or a long-context model family, some open models support extended context with segmented attention, others require custom batching. there are tradeoffs on latency and cost.
01:28 Peter: when you say KV cache, do you mean the kot-v cache?
01:31 Marco: oh sorry, k v cache, key-value cache, sometimes transcripts transcribed as KV cash in notes hehe. it helps keep prefix tokens in memory so you don't have to re-process entire history each request.
01:45 Dana: are there open models that natively do 100k? we prefer open models but if hosted with redwood provides better perf we can evaluate.
01:54 Marco: currently model families like LongForm-xxL and some Llama-extended variants handle very long contexts when compiled with windowed attention and optimized kernels. Redwood's runtime can route to quantized variants for cost-savings. for strict low-latency we often see dedicated capacity with pinned GPUs is best. hosted is simpler but might hit burst limits.
02:18 Sofia: what about multilingual quality? we have Spanish/Portuguese/Japanese, and also mixtures in same convo.
02:25 Marco: multilingual is model-dependent. Some open models are trained multilingual and do well; others are primarily english. we recommend A/B tests - you can run a subset against Anthropic/OPENAI too as baseline, but for private/open models we have verified profiles in our catalog. quick note: model naming in our catalog might be slightly different than upstream names sometimes.
02:48 Peter: tool calling - we need function-calling style structured responses for CRM lookups and to trigger actions. how mature is that across open families?
02:58 Marco: function or tool calling support varies. a few open models support the same structured output patterns, but often you need a shim that validates outputs and maps them to your tool schema. Redwood's hosted API supports streaming + structured outputs and function-call hooks. for private you can run the same runtime and handlers in your VPC. there can be slight differences in behavior across model variants so we recommend running the same prompt/test-set during benchmark.
03:26 Dana: security - SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs - we can't send PII to hosted without encryption at rest and clear audit trail.
03:35 Aisha: yes, we have SOC2 and ISO artifacts, SAML/SSO with SCIM provisioning, and customer-managed KMS for Private deployments. our dedicated offering includes isolated GPU pools and logs. will send security pack.
03:49 Sofia: do you support on-prem? sometimes regulated customers need air-gapped options.
03:53 Marco: yes, we have a private deployment offering that can be on-prem or VPC with optional air-gapped packaging for regulated workloads. there are additional ops costs.
04:10 Peter: latency vs cost - what numbers should we expect? if we use a quantized long-context model on dedicated, what's the per-1000-token cost ballpark versus hosted standard?
04:22 Marco: rough numbers, ballpark only: hosted with high-perf model maybe $0.005 per 1k tokens, dedicated quantized could be 30-50% lower depending on batching/cache, but you pay reserved capacity. private on-prem depends on your infra amortization. we'll include an apples-to-apples pricing sheet.
04:40 Dana: are there any gotchas around fallback? if dedicated pool saturates, can requests fall back to hosted variant automatically?
04:47 Marco: yes we support smart routing and automated fallback policies; you can set cost vs latency priorities. when falling back the model may be a different variant so we recommend prompt/regression tests.
04:59 Peter: ok good. also curious about evals for hallucination on long context, how do you recommend monitoring?
05:06 Marco: set up eval suites and prompt-based regression alerts. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization and batching settings, and you can tie quality alerts to prompt sets so if hallucination rises after a model version change you get notified.
05:22 Dana: competitor question - we're also talking to Anthropic and OpenAI. how does Redwood help reduce lock-in?
05:29 Aisha: our approach is to abstract deployment and provide consistent API/rollout primitives; you can pin model versions and route across model providers. that helps portability. we also support open models so you can host the same family in your private estate.
05:44 Sofia: networking - we need VPC peering and static IP ranges for firewalls.
05:49 Aisha: noted, will get networking doc and IP ranges.
05:53 Dana: ok next steps?
05:55 Aisha: recap: we'll run a benchmark on your 3 sample transcripts (you'll confirm list), we'll send SOC2/security pack, pricing for hosted vs dedicated and trial dedicated quote. marco will suggest model families for long context and share notes on tool-calling best practices.
06:12 Dana: sounds good. thanks everyone.

End of call.

Notes on transcription quality: medium - occasional mis-hearings (k v vs kv, vendor names capitalizations).

Shared artifacts referenced: pricing-sheet.xlsx (link in chat), security-pack.zip (link), sample-transcripts.tar.gz (customer provided link)
